messages:
Maria G: Heads up — customer-gaia reported missing tenant_id in nested 'events[].actor' when delivered to Splunk via webhook. They only see tenant_id on top-level but in our nested objects we omitted it. Repro steps: send webhook -> Splunk index shows actor without tenant_id. Anyone seen this before?

Jonah K: hmm. We relied on top-level tenant scoping. Downstream consumers apparently expect tenant_id on every event object. We should probably propagate it during serialization rather than force each downstream to join.

Ashley P: can you paste a minimal example of what they received vs what we emitted?

Maria G: sure, here's what the webhook payload looked like on their side:
```json
{"tenant_id":"gaia-42","events":[{"type":"login","actor":{"id":"u-123","email":"alice@example.com"},"ts":1679000000}]}
```
They say Splunk shows the actor object but no tenant_id under actor (so it's hard to filter by tenant in some alerts).

DevOps Sam: Splunk doesn't drop nested fields by itself. Most likely our webhook transform flattens into dotpaths and strips keys not whitelisted. Check ingest transform: /pkg/audit/transform.go — we have a filter that only copies top-level fields + events[].type|ts.

Jonah K: Plan: 1) serializer change to propagate top-level tenant_id into any nested object that looks like an entity (actor, resource, subject). 2) Add config flag config.audit.propagate_tenant (default true for Hosted). 3) Bump audit schema to v3 and include explicit note that tenant_id will be present on nested entities. 4) Add unit + integration tests that validate webhook, s3 export, and splunk mapping.

Ashley P: Also customer asked about KMS envelope provenance for S3 exports — they want the kms key-id surfaced in manifests and webhook metadata so their SIEM can correlate which key was used for each export. Can we add `kms_key_id` in the s3 manifest and a header `X-Redwood-KMS-Key` on webhook deliveries?

DevOps Sam: yes, s3-manifest writer already includes encryption metadata but we only send the KMS ARN in internal logs. I'll add a `kms_key_id` field to the manifest and surface a short key-id in the webhook header. Need to check with compliance for exposing that.

Jonah K: I'll open the serializer PR with tests. Will also add a migration section to the changelog describing consumer impact (no breaking changes for existing consumers, but nested tenant_id is new). I'll namespace the schema as `audit.v3` and add a compatibility note for older webhook clients.

Maria G: action items: Jonah -> PR for serializer + unit tests; Ashley -> docs update + customer notice + sample payloads for Splunk and Datadog; DevOps Sam -> add kms_key_id in manifest writer + webhook header; Compliance -> quick review (Ashley to ping). ETA: EOW for PRs, docs early next week. @ingest-bot please create INC ticket so CS has a tracking id.

ingest-bot: Incident created: INC-4821 — "Customer Gaia: tenant_id propagation & KMS metadata for audit exports" (assignee: Jonah K, priority: P2).

Jonah K: created PR -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/6123 (WIP). Tests added for webhook + s3 manifest; feature flag set to off for private installs.

Ashley P: I'll draft the customer note and sample payloads and drop them into the onboarding doc. Also adding a short Datadog example for their logs ingestion.

Maria G: great, thanks everyone. Please post PR links here when ready. :thumbsup:
